_notes: THE CONTACT BURST, ALONE. wind_contact_8f.png is 1774x887 over 4x2, same
non-dividing sheet shape and the same README-stated boundaries as the rest
of the pack (x: 0, 444, 887, 1331, 1774; y: 0, 444, 887). Explicit rects,
for the same reason water's and fire's notes give.
THE SEQUENCE: c0 a small approaching swirl (the same role as water's
contact_f0 and fire's -- the played layer starts at startFrame 2 to skip it).
c1 a growing swirl. c2 an opening ring. c3 is the WIDEST frame -- 17.9% ink,
runner-up c4 at 14.7% -- a full open double-ring pressure ring, source frame
4 one-indexed, the same peak position as fire's and water's own contact_f3.
c4 a dispersing flower/pinwheel read (large but slightly less ink than c3).
c5-c7 thin the ring into trailing wisps; c7 is nearly gone.
A REAL DEFECT: c3, the peak frame, TOUCHES THE BOTTOM EDGE of its own cell --
confirmed visually, the ring's lower arc is cut by the sheet's own delivered
boundary, not by this recipe's slicing. c7 likewise touches the top edge (a
thin trailing wisp, cosmetically minor). Because c3's clipping is baked into
the source pixels, no rect or canvas choice here recovers it -- it is reported
rather than worked around. GIVEN THE CLIP, c3 gets hold: 2 for weight but NO
scale growth (unlike fire's and water's matching hold+scale step): growing an
already-clipped frame about its own centre would clip further, not just add
size.
CANVAS 512, same headroom reasoning as the rest of the pack -- the split-per-
layer recipe's own largest cell is 444, so padding is stated rather than
inferred.
